senses.en_definition: Used up, eaten up, sold out, or otherwise gone, with none remaining.
For the most part; almost entirely; over a large area.
Spent, used, or taken up by something, especially of money or time.

collocations.en: taken up by the opening remarks

senses.en_definition: Most; to the highest degree, used before an adjective to form a superlative.
Then; in that case, introducing a follow-up question or conclusion.
After; following the completion of an action; then.
Well, because; used informally to introduce a reason or justification.

collocations.en: well, because I keep getting yelled at
well, I don't have a choice

messages.en: I've finished eating. Where are you? Want to meet in the lobby?
I'm still at the bookshop. Give me five minutes and I'll come down.
Want to go for lunch now? I'm hungry already.
Finish that work first, okay? There's only a little left.

senses.en_definition: The front; the part or area opposite the back.

messages.en: Shall we meet at our usual café next week? I want to talk about the new project.
Sure. Are you free on Tuesday at three?

senses.en_definition: A gift given as a token of appreciation, remembrance, respect, or good wishes.
A prize, in money or another form, awarded for winning a competition or in recognition of achievement.

messages.en: Have you bought Nisa a present yet? I'm going to get a cake this evening.
Yep, I got her that bag she likes. Don't tell her yet, okay? It'll spoil the surprise.
Okay, my lips are sealed. You bring the present tomorrow, and I'll bring the cake.
